input.quote: 15.16 Nonsolicitation. During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant with the soliciting Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website.
input.rationale: Section 15.16 sits at our fallback position rather than the preferred "no non-solicit on PB", and is acceptable as drafted. It is mutual ("neither Party"), scope-limited to employees who are or have been involved in the performance or oversight of the development activities (not all personnel), contains an express general-advertising/generalized-search carve-out, and prohibits only solicitation to terminate employment — there is no no-hire covenant, so it is well clear of walk-away territory. Two minor sub-elements short of the fallback wording are noted but not flagged: there is no express carve-out for unsolicited approaches by the employee, and the tail period is redacted ([***] after the Term), which should be confirmed at 12 months or less measured from the end of the individual's involvement; anything above 24 months would need to be revisited.
